body.statement:
Fix an admissible query \(z_0\).  Every kernel \(\mathbb P_{z_0}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}\!\left[
 \left\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\right\}W
 \right]=0
\]
for every cohort \(s\), unit \(i\), and bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable random variable \(W\).  Hence each \(E\in\mathcal X\) with \(0<\mathbb P_{z_0}(E)<1\) has the same treated mean on \(E\) and \(E^c\), and \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} excludes the former common-design-shock kernel.  For each \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), these conclusions transfer to \(P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\) for \(P\)-almost every query \(z_0\), with no assertion at query-null versions.  Nevertheless, there are admissible scalar fixed class parameters and, for every positive \(N,T,n_1\), two kernels \(\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)},\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0)\), with corresponding degenerate-query laws \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\), having the same joint law of \((X_{1t},Q_{1ti},Z_j)\) and the same target \(\tau(z_0)=0\), while
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus removal of the invalid witness is a necessary model repair, not a determination of the sharp constants for the remaining centered fixed-query product experiment.
body.justification: The theorem records exactly what centering rules out on the fixed-query class and supplies an explicit two-kernel variance certificate, then transfers the audit to panel laws only almost everywhere.
body.gap: Exact constants for the remaining centered fixed-query optimal-recovery product experiment remain open.
body.consumer: The model audit removes the obsolete negative answer without overstating centering or selecting a null conditional version.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(z_0\) and \(\mathbb P_{z_0}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), and put
\[
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}].
\]
Bounded wealth and consistency give \(|B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) almost surely, so \(\mu_{si}\) is finite.  The design-conditional-centering clause of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid\mathcal X]=0.
\tag{1}
\]
For bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable \(W\), the pull-out and tower properties of conditional expectation yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W]
 &=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid\mathcal X)
 \right]\\
 &=0.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
This proves the asserted orthogonality.

Let \(E\in\mathcal X\) and set \(p_E=\mathbb P_{z_0}(E)\).  Taking \(W=\mathbf 1_E\) in (2) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E]=\mu_{si}p_E.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(p_E>0\), division by \(p_E\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E]=\mu_{si}.
\tag{4}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{z_0}}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E^c]=\mu_{si}
\tag{5}
\]
when \(p_E<1\).  Equations (4)--(5) hold simultaneously for \(0<p_E<1\), and \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} gives the stated exclusion.  By \texttt{lem:panel-fixed-query-kernel-transfer}, every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) has a regular conditional kernel in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost every query.  Applying (1)--(5) to those kernels proves the panel-to-kernel transfer and makes no claim at a null-version query.

We now construct the two fixed-query kernels.  For arbitrary positive integers \(N,T,n_1\), take
\[
 S=1,
 \quad \pi_1=1,
 \quad H=0,
 \quad p=d=1,
 \quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,
 \quad B=L=1,
 \quad \delta_0=\frac14,
\tag{6}
\]
and set \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), with any fixed \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  These values satisfy all declared parameter ranges, and \(d=p(H+1)=1\).

On a product probability space let \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T}\), \((\xi_j)_{j=1}^{N}\), and \((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}\) be mutually independent, with
\[
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\xi_j=1)=\mathbb P(\xi_j=-1)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=1)=\mathbb P(\varepsilon_i=-1)=\frac12.
\tag{7}
\]
Define
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12,
 \qquad
 Z_j=\frac12+\xi_j.
\tag{8}
\]
For every event unit set \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).  Definition \texttt{def:buyhold-level} gives
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.
\tag{9}
\]
Under \(\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\); under \(\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In each case impose consistency by setting \(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  Then
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12
 \quad\text{under }\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)},
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}.
\tag{10}
\]
The smallest constructed return is \(-1/2>-1\), as required by the return support.

We verify membership in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0)\).  Equations (8)--(10) imply
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
\tag{11}
\]
so bounded wealth holds.  The constant \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\), zero first derivative, and zero Holder seminorm; hence \(m_1\in\mathcal H_1(1,1)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_{1t\mid z_0}(x)=1
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1].
\tag{12}
\]
Thus interior support and the query-conditional density bound hold.  The design dates are independent, so
\[
 \beta_1(k\mid z_0)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1.
\tag{13}
\]

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T})\).  Training outcomes are deterministic, and under the second kernel unit \(i\)'s event history depends only on \(\varepsilon_i\).  Independence in (7) therefore gives conditional independence of unit histories across \(i\), while
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{1ti}\mid\mathcal X]=\frac12=m_1(X_{1t}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =\mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}].
\tag{14}
\]
Exact observation of each \(X_{1t}\) gives the center-only design property.  The donor sigma-field is generated by \((\xi_j)_j\), whereas the complete joint panel is generated by \((X_{1t})_t\) and, under the second kernel, \((\varepsilon_i)_i\).  Mutual independence in (7) therefore proves donor independence from the entire joint panel.

The donor conditions follow directly from (8):
\[
 \mathbb E Z_j=z_0=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j)=1,
 \qquad
 c_\Sigma I_1\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_1,
\tag{15}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4
 =\mathbb E|\xi_j|^4
 =1=B^4.
\tag{16}
\]
Finally, (9) and the definition of \(m_1\) give
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{1i}(0)]=\frac12=m_1(z_0),
\tag{17}
\]
so event-date transport holds.  Equations (8)--(17), together with imposed consistency, verify every clause of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}; hence
\[
 \mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)},\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}
 \in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(z_0).
\tag{18}
\]
If the query variable is taken to equal \(1/2\) almost surely and the conditional kernels are (18), the resulting laws \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\) satisfy every member property in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}; all query-conditional requirements are checked at their sole positive-probability query.  Thus \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\), without any appeal to a null conditional version.

The joint law of \(((X_{1t})_t,(Q_{1ti})_{t,i},(Z_j)_j)\) is common to the two kernels by (7)--(8).  By \texttt{def:target}, (9)--(10), and \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]=0,\\
 \tau_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)]
 =\frac14\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
Nevertheless, (10) and independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb P_{z_0}^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X)
 =\frac1{16}\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)
 =\frac1{16}.
\tag{20}
\]
Thus the fixed-query centered class permits different event-noise constants while holding the training experiment, donor experiment, and causal target fixed.  This proves the explicit certificate and the stated distinction between excluding the obsolete common-design shock and calculating a sharp minimax constant.
